title: Learning to Reduce Search Space for Generalizable Neural Routing Solver

problem.claim: Scaling neural combinatorial optimization methods to large-scale vehicle routing instances is computationally challenging.

gap.claim: Existing geometric distance-based dynamic search-space reduction methods can struggle with non-uniform distributions and instances where optimal solutions depend heavily on non-spatial constraints.

contributions.claim: L2R is a learning-based dynamic search-space reduction framework for neural routing solvers.
L2R adaptively prioritizes nodes using problem-specific features to prune the search space during solution construction.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report robust generalization across problem scales and data distributions on various vehicle routing problem variants.
The authors report that L2R scales to vehicle routing instances with 10 million nodes while maintaining high solution quality.

narrative_sequence.summary: Neural combinatorial optimization can construct approximate vehicle-routing solutions while reducing reliance on expert algorithm design.
Large-scale instances remain difficult because of high computational complexity.
Existing dynamic search-space reduction based on geometric distance can fail on complex or non-spatially constrained instances.
L2R learns from problem-specific features to prioritize nodes and prune the search space dynamically.
The authors report robust generalization and scaling to 10 million-node instances with high solution quality.

source_observation.claim: Search-space reduction can be learned from problem-specific features rather than relying only on geometric distance.

interpretation.claim: Feature-adaptive pruning may better accommodate heterogeneous data and non-spatial constraints.

application.claim: Use problem-specific signals to prioritize candidates when designing scalable constructive solvers.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach improves every routing variant or constraint regime.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the model architecture, training procedure, datasets, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not define the supported vehicle routing variants or the meaning of high solution quality.
